title.narrative: Enhancing the Sustainable Return of Returnees in Deir-ez-Zor through Shelter Rehabilitation, Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance, and Protection Services.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project contributes Supporting Safe and Dignified Return from Areas of Displacement to Areas of Origin, aiming to ensure that returnees and host communities in Deir-ez-Zor have equitable access to protection, essential services, and multi-purpose cash assistance , voluntary, and dignified return.ltbrgtThe project addresses the critical barriers facing over one million returnees across Syria—particularly in Deir-ez-Zor—such as damaged housing, inadequate services, protection risks, and economic vulnerability. Drawing on findings from the 2025 WoS Rapid Needs Assessment (RNA), the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO 2025), and direct field consultations, the project will implement a multi-sectoral package of shelter rehabilitation, cash-based assistance, and protection services to enhance the reintegration environment and reduce dependency on humanitarian aid.ltbrgtThe intervention targets 8,293 recently returned individuals in Deir-ez-Zor, which corresponds to approximately 1,600 returnee families.ltbrgt neighborhoods with visible return movement: Al-Huwayqa, Al-Rashdiya, Al-Omal, Al-Sinaa, Al-Matar Al-Qadeem, Al-Hamidiya, Al-Jbeila, Al-Arfi, Al-Muwazzafeen, and Al-KanamatiltbrgtBeneficiary selection is based on clearly defined vulnerability criteria, including:ltbrgt1. Returnees who have returned within the last six months.ltbrgt2. Households headed by widows.ltbrgt3. Households including persons with disabilities.ltbrgt4. Households with elderly members over the age of 70.ltbrgt5. Families with people with chronic diseases such as cancerltbrgt-To ensure transparency, coordination, and accountability, the project will establish joint technical and social assessment committees, composed of representatives from the Deir-ez-Zor Governorate, Directorate of Technical Services (specialized engineers), and the Directorate of Social Affairs and Labor And an engineer from the municipality. These committees will carry out:ltbrgt Technical assessments of shelter damage levels using a standardized form (minor, moderate)ltbrgtKey components include:ltbrgt-Shelter and Non-Food Items (55%): Rehabilitation of returnee homes categorized by the level of structural damage, as identified through the technical assessment process. The intervention will ensure safe and dignified living conditions and improve tenure security for vulnerable households.ltbrgt- Rehabilitation and maintenance of homes with minor damage:ltbrgt300 shelters will be rehabilitated in accordance with Shelter/NFI sector technical standards, with a maximum repair cost of $800 per unit.ltbrgt-Rehabilitation and maintenance of homes with moderate damage:ltbrgt200 shelters will be rehabilitated in accordance with Shelter/NFI sector technical standards, with a maximum repair cost of $2,500 per unit.ltbrgt- Multi-purpose cash assistance (23%): conditional cash assistance will be provided to selected returnee households to meet their immediate needs, including food, healthcare, hygiene kits, and essential non-food items. Each household will receive US$100 in cash, enabling immediate stabilization, enhancing dignity, and stimulating the recovery of local markets in areas of return. six times every monthA, in installments of $100, equivalent to 500 families. with Al-Haram or Al-Fouad, available in Deir ez-Zor.ltbrgt-Protection (22%):ltbrgt1. Capacity Building of Protection Actors Provide tailored services to GBV survivors, including case managementltbrgt 2. Mobile Safe Spaces for Women and Children, Establish mobile safe spaces dedicated to women, girls, and children, including Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS).ltbrgt 3. Integrated Protection Monitoring System Monitor protection risks in high-risk areas, including housing, land, and property (HLP) disputes, explosive ordnance (EO) contamination, and discrimination against returnees.ltbrgt4. Comprehensive Prevention and Response Package Conduct community-based awareness campaigns on legal rights, explosive ordnance risks, and peaceful coexistence.ltbrgt5. Specialized Services for High-Risk Groups: Provide tailored services to GBV survivors, including case management.ltbrgtlt/pgt
